audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant penult (strict=false) with domain ROOT/STEM rather than WORD, and a caution listing the morphologically/grammatically conditioned final stress; or 'morphological' if the catalog follows its own precedent for root-penult-plus-stress-attracting-suffix systems (Luang luan1263 and Takivatan Bunun bunu1267 are coded 'morphological' on near-identical statements).
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every quoted sentence is verbatim in the held Mettler & Mettler 1990 scan at pp.44-45. The source is the right one (only dedicated phonology; endorsed as such by Visser 2024, also held). But the coding 'fixed-strict, penult, domain WORD' over-reads it. Mettler 1990 itself says stress is penult OF THE ROOT, that personal prefixes are never stressed (ku-'min, mu-'fla = final stress on disyllabic words), and that plural -ar takes the stress after non-e-final roots (lend'nar, as'war, sor'yar = final stress); §7.3 adds shifts 'to the ultimate syllable' from vowel deletion and phrase stress, 'in particular for verbs'. Rumyaru & Mettler 1999 §1.5 (fetched sources now) repeats all of this with accent-marked forms (kumín, muflá, bulnár, aswár). sources.quote: §32: 'De klemtoon valt altijd op den wortel en niet op den uitgang. Alleen om grammatikale redenen kan hij in stammen met gesloten wortel en gesloten uitgang verspringen op den uitgang.' (Stress always falls on the root [= first syllable of the disyllabic stem, i.e. penult] and not on the ending; only for grammatical reasons can it jump to the ending in stems with closed root and closed ending.) §§33-38 then list the grammatical shifts to the FINAL syllable: §33 ambitransitive verbs used intransitively ('nmalip jak' he laughs at me vs nma'lip he laughs; kamta'sing we weep); §34 stative/'neuter
sources.locator: Hoofdstuk IV 'De Klemtoon', §§32-38, pp.12-14 (with §15 p.7 defining 'wortel' = first and 'uitgang' = second syllable of the disyllabic stem)

sources.quote: §1.5.1: 'Setiap bentuk kata dasar/akar kata yang belum dimodifikasi, tekanan kata selalu jatuh pada suku kedua dari akhir kata. Tekanan kata tersebut tidak fonemis' (in every unmodified base/root, stress always falls on the second syllable from the end; not phonemic): léte, katútun, ásu, léndan. Person prefixes on verbs/adjectives are never stressed: kumín 'I stay', muflá 'you run', mimpán, mamín, raflá, kufínau. §1.5.2: no shift when plural -ar is added to e-final roots (léte > létar, dóle > dólar); otherwise 'Tekanan kata akan berpindah ke afiks jamak' (stress moves to the plural affix): búl
